findings.quote: Saffire-I burned for 400 sec • Saffire-III burned for 320 sec. ♦This is equal to the inverse ratio of the flame speed
findings.about: Burn times of Saffire-I and -III are in the inverse ratio of their flame speeds (NASA's next line: flame speed proportional to air flow, Saffire-III 25 cm/s, Saffire-I 20 cm/s)
findings.note: PSI's Saffire-III table gives 30 cm/s, not 25.

findings.quote: Flame spread over a large thin charring surface in low-gravity showed that steady flame spread was possible (unlike normal gravity).
findings.about: Steady flame spread over a large thin charring fabric in low gravity, unlike at 1 g

findings.quote: Concurrent flame spread (with the wind) was shown to be more sensitive to the flow duct dimension than previously anticipated.
findings.about: Concurrent spread depends on the flow duct size more than expected

findings.quote: they determined that concurrent flames can achieve a steady spread rate and that overall the concurrent spread rates are strongly influenced the the flow duct size.
findings.about: Concurrent flames reach a steady spread rate; the rate depends strongly on duct size

findings.quote: Average flame spread rate is 1.8 mm/s; estimated average flame power is 1200 +/- 300 W Total burn time is 420 s
findings.about: Saffire-I concurrent burn of the 40.6 x 94 cm fabric: average flame spread rate
findings.note: SIBAL fabric (40.6 cm x 94 cm) burning in air at 20 cm/s concurrent flow (same slide).

findings.about: Saffire-I concurrent burn: total burn time

findings.quote: Average flame spread rate is 1.8 mm/s; estimated average flame power is 1200 +/- 300 W Total burn time is 420 s
findings.about: Saffire-I concurrent burn: estimated average flame power, 1200 +/- 300 W (no site variable)

findings.quote: For the concurrent flame, the length reaches a plateau value of around 40 mm, while the opposed-flow flame is a bit shorter at 24 mm.
findings.about: Saffire-I flame length: plateau of about 40 mm (concurrent) and 24 mm (opposed) (no site variable)

findings.quote: The flame spread rate for the 5-cm-wide sample is marginally faster compared to the spread rate for the 40.6-cm-wide sample for the same flow speed of 20 cm/s (2.1 compared to 1.8 mm/s). ‒ This is partly due to the slightly higher starting oxygen percentage (22.1% vs. 21.7%).
findings.about: Narrow (5 cm, Saffire-II 2-5) fabric spread faster than the wide (40.6 cm, Saffire-I) fabric at 20 cm/s
findings.note: value_num is the 5-cm-wide sample's rate; the 40.6-cm-wide rate is 1.8 mm/s.

findings.quote: About 90% of the fuel burned in the first test leaving 10% unburned, allowing a meaningful opposed-flow test to be completed.
findings.about: Saffire-I: share of the large sample burned in the concurrent test

findings.quote: At first, the flame length and brightness varied significantly at a periodic frequency of about 1.4 Hz before finally becoming more stable at about 90 s into the test.
findings.about: Saffire-I concurrent flame pulsated at about 1.4 Hz for the first 90 s (no site variable)

findings.quote: Unlike 1-g, the results revealed that a steady flame could be achieved even for a wide sample burning in concurrent-flow.
findings.about: A wide concurrent-flow flame reached a steady state in microgravity, unlike at 1 g

findings.quote: The flames spread more slowly than prior tests in smaller ducts. This behavior of the flame demonstrated the importance of confined spaces for potential spacecraft fires.
findings.about: Saffire flames spread more slowly than in earlier tests in smaller ducts
